_note: The stages Adaptation may use when it plans by realization (realization.md, Step 2). One stage = one kind of thinking (rule R3). Code reads this file: the planner's stage table is rendered from it, the plan check allows only these ids, and the Map names each stage's role and box from it. Fields: thinking (what the stage decides), tiers (realization.md tiers it covers), output (what its workflows produce), role (who does it: the workflow agent works as this role, and the Map names it), skill (optional: the skill file, under agents/j2/, the workflow agent follows), verb (what the role does), approach (a standard method), use_when (when a brief needs it), note (limits). Use only the stages a brief needs.

stages.thinking: Money and position: business model, revenue, cost, edge, goals as numbers
stages.approach: Business model canvas; unit economics; goals stated as numbers with a date
stages.use_when: The brief has a commercial goal, a business model, a target or investors

stages.thinking: The market: size, segments, competitors, trends, willingness to pay
stages.approach: Market sizing (total, serviceable, obtainable); competitor matrix; price benchmarks; every figure with its source
stages.use_when: Positioning, pricing, a target or a plan depends on the market or competitors
stages.note: Needs outside sources. Without web access, figures come from memory and are marked to be confirmed

stages.thinking: The people: needs, behaviour, pain points, context of use
stages.approach: Jobs to be done; personas built from evidence; journey map
stages.use_when: Who the users are, or what they need, is unclear or disputed
stages.note: Without real users, write assumptions to test, not findings

stages.thinking: What is possible or true in the domain: feasibility, evidence, known methods
stages.approach: Evidence review; a small proof-of-concept; confidence stated for each conclusion
stages.use_when: A method or a claim must be shown to work before anything is built on it
stages.note: Needs outside sources for evidence; without web access, mark conclusions to be confirmed

stages.thinking: Money flows: budget, pricing, forecasts, payback, funding
stages.approach: Driver-based model (inputs, calculations, outputs); scenarios; sensitivity table
stages.use_when: The output has a budget, a price, a projection, a payback or a funding ask

stages.thinking: Rights and obligations: contracts, terms, licences, intellectual property, trademarks
stages.approach: List each obligation and right; draft the terms; flag what a lawyer must review
stages.use_when: Terms, licences, trademarks, contracts or disclaimers are part of the output
stages.note: Mark the result as not legal advice

stages.thinking: Rules from outside: law, regulator, licence, privacy, tax, platform policy
stages.approach: List the rules that apply; map each rule to a requirement; cite the rule
stages.use_when: A law, regulator, tax rule, licence or platform policy applies to the output
stages.note: Rule details from memory are marked to be confirmed

stages.thinking: Risk and threats: security, privacy, safety, abuse, failure
stages.approach: Threat model (assets, threats, controls); risk register with likelihood and impact
stages.use_when: Personal data, payments, safety, children or possible abuse are involved

stages.thinking: Users and scope: who, which jobs, what is in and out, in what order
stages.approach: Story mapping; prioritised scope (must, should, could); acceptance criteria
stages.use_when: The output has users who do something with it

stages.thinking: Experience: flows, layout, look, interaction, accessibility
stages.approach: User flows; layouts per screen width; style guide (colour, type, spacing); accessibility rules
stages.use_when: People see or use the output

stages.thinking: Identity and voice: name, personality, visual identity, tone
stages.approach: Positioning; personality in three words; voice with do and don't examples; logo and palette rules
stages.use_when: The brief asks for a name, a brand, a voice, or a new business's identity

stages.thinking: Words and media: what is said, its structure and tone
stages.approach: Content outline; style guide; a fixed word list the builders use exactly
stages.use_when: The output is mostly words or media, or the words decide whether it works

stages.thinking: Teaching: learning outcomes, sequence, practice, assessment
stages.approach: Backward design: outcomes first, then how they are assessed, then the lessons
stages.use_when: The output teaches or trains someone

stages.thinking: Measurement and data: what to collect, metrics, data model, analysis
stages.approach: Metric tree from the goal; data dictionary; the right chart for each question
stages.use_when: The output collects, analyses or shows data, or success must be measured

stages.thinking: Structure: components, interfaces, data model, scale (high-level and low-level design)
stages.approach: High-level design (components, how they connect), then low-level design (interfaces, data, rules); non-functional needs
stages.use_when: The output is software with more than one part, or has data, scale or integration needs

stages.thinking: AI behaviour: what the model does, its prompts or data, how it is evaluated
stages.approach: Task definition; prompt or model choice; test set with expected answers; what it does when it fails
stages.use_when: The output uses a language model, a chatbot or any learned model

stages.thinking: Making the thing: the code, page, app or document itself
stages.approach: Build to the earlier stages' outputs; one section per workflow, checked by code
stages.use_when: Always, when something is made

stages.thinking: What to buy or use and from whom: vendors, tools, services, materials
stages.approach: Requirements; shortlist; comparison matrix with cost and risk
stages.use_when: The output depends on outside vendors, tools, services or materials

stages.thinking: Physical making at scale: process, capacity, cost per unit, quality at source
stages.approach: Bill of materials; process flow; capacity and cost per unit
stages.use_when: A physical product is made

stages.thinking: Fitting other languages, regions and abilities
stages.approach: String list; translation; local formats (dates, money, numbers); accessibility (WCAG)
stages.use_when: The output must work in more than one language or region, or for people with disabilities

stages.thinking: Tests that are part of the deliverable: test cases, expected results, acceptance
stages.approach: Test cases derived from the done-when items, each with its expected result
stages.use_when: A test set or test plan is itself a done-when item
stages.note: Checking J2's own output is Audit's job: never plan a check or review workflow

stages.thinking: Running it every day: deployment, processes, monitoring
stages.approach: Runbook; release checklist; who does what, every day
stages.use_when: The output must be deployed, run or operated after it is made

stages.thinking: Moving physical goods: shipping, stock, delivery, returns
stages.approach: Shipping zones and carriers; delivery times and charges; returns flow
stages.use_when: Physical goods are stored, shipped or returned

stages.thinking: Positioning, message and channels: what we say, to whom, where
stages.approach: Positioning statement; key messages; channel plan with budget and targets; calendar
stages.use_when: The output must reach, persuade or win people: a launch, a campaign, a content plan

stages.thinking: Measured experiments to raise acquisition, activation and retention
stages.approach: Funnel metrics; one hypothesis per experiment; a test with a success line
stages.use_when: Success depends on numbers that only trying can move (sign-ups, retention)

stages.thinking: Converting and closing: pipeline, offers, objections
stages.approach: Ideal customer profile; pipeline stages; pitch and objection handling
stages.use_when: The output must win paying customers through direct contact

stages.thinking: Working through others: partners, integrations, affiliates
stages.approach: Partner map; what each side gives and gets; terms
stages.use_when: The output depends on partners, integrations or affiliates

stages.thinking: Helping people after they start: answers, issues, escalation
stages.approach: Top questions with answers; escalation paths; response times
stages.use_when: Users will need help, answers or a way to complain

stages.thinking: Teaching users or staff to use what was made
stages.approach: Step-by-step guides; walkthroughs; onboarding checklist
stages.use_when: Users or staff must learn to use or run the output

stages.thinking: Keeping it working: reliability, updates, incidents
stages.approach: Monitoring; incident response; update schedule
stages.use_when: The output must keep running and be updated over time

stages.thinking: Who does the work: roles, hiring, policies, workplace law
stages.approach: Roles and responsibilities; policies; processes; the labour law that applies
stages.use_when: The output is about staff, hiring, roles or workplace policy

stages.thinking: Who decides and how: approvals, ownership, reviews
stages.approach: Decision rights; approval steps; review cycle
stages.use_when: The output itself is a governance document or decision process
stages.note: J2's own functions already govern the run; don't plan governance of J2's work

stages.thinking: Environmental and social impact
stages.approach: Impact areas; measures; targets with dates
stages.use_when: The brief asks about environmental or social impact, or a rule requires it
